sections.h2: Where do I pay property tax in White County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Pay the White County Tax Commissioner at 506 North Main Street in Cleveland, by mail to P. O. Box 970, Cleveland, GA 30528, or online. The phone number is 706-865-2225. The drive-thru runs 8 am to 4:30 pm and the lobby 8 am to 4:50 pm, Monday through Friday.

The county site says bills go out each August and are due November 15, and that cash, check or card are accepted in person, with convenience fees on card and online payments. The commissioner's office bills and collects tax on timber, real and personal property, mobile homes, utilities and motor vehicles. It also acts as the state's agent for vehicle registration.

The Tax Assessor's Office is a different counter, in Suite 180 of the White County Mauney Building. The Board of Assessors meets there on the second Wednesday of each month at 9 a.m. to discuss appeals, homestead exemptions and other changes in taxation status.

sections.h2: What makes White County different from its neighbors?
sections.html:
White County covers 240.74 square miles of land and counted 116.3 people per square mile in 2020. The Census Bureau estimates 29,802 people for July 2025, 6.4% more than the April 2020 base. The county site lists Cleveland, Helen and Sautee Nacoochee as its communities.

The recreation list on that site includes Anna Ruby Falls, Dukes Creek Falls, Hardman Farm State Historic Site, Smithgall Woods State Park and Unicoi State Park and Lodge. Schools are run by the White County School System. The Census figures for the county follow.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $278,900 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 78.8%, from 14,547 housing units.
  • Median gross rent: $1,032, and 190 building permits were issued in 2025.
  • Residents 65 and older: 25.4%, with a mean commute of 30.4 minutes.
  • Median household income: $70,666 in 2024 dollars.

The Census Bureau also counts 10,729 households for 2020 to 2024, with 2.63 people per household and 88.1% living in the same house a year earlier. A higher home value brings a larger tax bill, so a seller who carries unpaid years should plan for interest on a bigger balance. Ask the commissioner for a payoff that covers every open year before the house is listed.

sections.h2: How are White County property taxes calculated?
sections.html:
The county multiplies the assessed value, after exemptions, by the millage rate. Georgia assesses property at 40% of fair market value unless a rule says otherwise, and one mill equals one dollar per $1,000 of assessed value. The assessor sets value, and the taxing bodies set the rate.

The White County Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education are the main rate setters. A notice on the county home page for 2026 shows the commissioners planning to lower the county millage rate to 8.555 mills from 8.842 mills in 2025, a drop of 0.287 mills. That figure covers the county government, so school and city levies sit on top of it on your bill. Cleveland and Helen are separate cities, so ask the tax commissioner whether a city levy applies to your address.

Your property record is searchable by name or address on the county's property records site, which is also where the homestead application opens. Pull the record before you list so the owner name, acreage and exemptions match what you expect to sell.

Georgia owners file a return of real property between January 1 and April 1. If you skip it, the prior year's value counts as your return. After the return period the assessors mail an Annual Notice of Assessment showing last year's value, this year's value, an estimate of tax at last year's millage and the reason for any change.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a White County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date printed on the Annual Notice of Assessment, which White County usually mails in early May. The county lists six grounds: value, uniformity, taxability, denial of exemption, breach of covenant and denial of covenant. A tax bill itself cannot be appealed in Georgia.

The deadline is firm. The county says failing to appeal in the window waives the appeal for that year, and the Board of Assessors cannot make an exception. If you agree with the value on the notice, you do nothing.

The Board of Equalization is described on the county site as a special jury that hears appeals of property values and denials of homestead and other exemptions. Questions about it go to the White County Clerk of Court at 706-865-2613.

sections.h2: How do I get a homestead exemption in White County?
sections.html:
File with the county by April 1 for the current year, using the online application inside the property records site. The home must be your primary residence, and you cannot claim homestead in another county or state. A valid Georgia driver's license or ID showing your physical residence address is required.

Applications are taken all year, but a late one applies to the following year. The county says it has numerous homestead exemptions and points owners to the assessor for the list. Freeport exemption for inventory and conservation use assessment for farm and timber land are also on the exemptions page, and conservation use covers up to 2,000 acres under Georgia Code 48-5-7.4 with a ten-year covenant.

sections.h2: What happens if White County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes after November 15 bring penalties, and the steps escalate from fees to liens, levies and a tax sale. Payments are still accepted on a delinquent bill, but interest keeps accruing. A lien, also called a Fi. Fa., stays on record with the Clerk of Court for seven years and may hurt credit reports and ratings.

A levy seizes a portion of the property to cover the debt. The county says a sign may be posted and the owner can still live there. A tax sale is advertised for four consecutive weeks in the White County News and held on the first Tuesday of a month on the courthouse steps. Buyers pay with certified funds and get a Sheriff's tax deed.

The original owner has one year to redeem the property, and lien and mortgage holders may redeem too. After that year the buyer may foreclose the right of redemption. A seller with a lien should ask the commissioner for a written payoff figure and give it to the closing attorney so the lien is cleared at closing.

faqs.q: When are White County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due November 15. Bills are sent each August. Missing the date brings penalties, and interest keeps accruing on a delinquent bill.

faqs.q: How do I reach the White County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: Call 706-865-2225 or visit 506 North Main Street in Cleveland. The lobby is open 8 am to 4:50 pm Monday through Friday, and the drive-thru closes at 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a White County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment. The notice is usually mailed in early May. The Board of Assessors cannot extend that deadline.

faqs.q: What is the White County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: Apply by April 1 to receive the exemption for the current year. You can apply at any time, but a late application shifts the benefit to the next year. The home must be your primary residence.

faqs.q: Can a White County lien stop me from selling?
faqs.a: The county says a lien is removed by paying the delinquent balance with the associated fees and interest. Ask the commissioner for that payoff figure and hand it to the closing attorney.
